area: XAI + uncertainty quantification for cell/neurite segmentation models, scoped to a 2-person offline desktop app (no training stack at runtime)

candidates.name: Grad-CAM (pytorch-grad-cam)
candidates.what_it_does: Per-pixel class-activation maps at a chosen conv layer; for segmentation, target = logit of the class at a pixel/region (repo documents semantic-segmentation usage incl. SegEigenCAM for seg); also supports ViT encoders via reshape transforms
candidates.pc12_fit: Works on U-Net directly; for ViT (Cellpose/nnU-Net-ViT) need last-block target + reshape transform, more fiddly
candidates.neurite_support: Fine-resolution maps come from U-Net skip layers; choose a high-res decoder layer so thin neurite borders are resolved (low-res bottleneck layer misses tubular detail)
candidates.compute: 1 forward+backward per image; well under 2 s even on CPU for 2D 256-1024px crops; batched
candidates.small_data_fit: No training required — works on the models you already have
candidates.notes: Coarse at object level; use as the cheap fallback, not the headline method. Captum also has Grad-CAM (BSD-3, https://github.com/pytorch/captum).

candidates.name: Integrated Gradients (captum)
candidates.what_it_does: Axiom-satisfying per-pixel attributions; target = pixel logit (or masked-region loss) for segmentation; noise_tunnel option = SmoothGrad for cleaner maps
candidates.pc12_fit: Fully per-pixel, works for any differentiable U-Net; baseline = zero image; needs ~20-50 Riemann steps
candidates.neurite_support: Per-pixel resolution, so it tracks thin neurite boundaries better than CAM-style maps
candidates.compute: ~20-50 forward-backward passes per image; a few seconds on laptop GPU, tens of seconds on CPU — batch across crops
candidates.notes: Primary saliency method: faithful + cheap + gives clean per-pixel maps for the 'why was this pixel neurite?' overlay. Passes Adebayo sanity checks (unlike guided backprop).

candidates.name: Seg-Grad-CAM (Vinogradova et al., AAAI 2020)
candidates.what_it_does: Grad-CAM generalized to per-pixel segmentation targets; produces dense per-pixel explanation maps without pooling to a single class score
candidates.pc12_fit: Conceptually ideal for segmentation; NOT 'Bach et al.' (likely mis-remembered in the brief)
candidates.neurite_support: Dense maps; but only demoed on Cityscapes/TextureMNIST
candidates.license: LICENSE file present; terms not verified (repo is Keras, no PyTorch port)
candidates.notes: Official repo: Keras only, Python 3.6-era, README says 'no updates or upgrades planned'. Reimplementing in ~30 PyTorch lines is feasible but not worth the effort vs. per-pixel-target Integrated Gradients/Grad-CAM which give equivalent maps with maintained libraries.

candidates.name: RISE / occlusion
candidates.what_it_does: Black-box: probe model with ~100 random masks, aggregate saliency; also the deletion/insertion protocol itself
candidates.pc12_fit: Works through ONNX export — useful to prove the exported model behaves identically to the PyTorch model
candidates.neurite_support: Mask granularity determines; fine enough for neurites with small masks
candidates.compute: ~100 forward passes per image; offline/development use, NOT per-image in the app
candidates.notes: Use only in the saliency-validation protocol (as occlusion ground truth) and as an ONNX-consistency check — not the shipped XAI layer.

candidates.name: Deep ensemble (5 members from 5 CV folds)
candidates.what_it_does: Mean + variance of per-pixel softmax across 5 independently trained models = epistemic uncertainty map; standard technique per Lakshminarayanan et al. NIPS 2017
candidates.pc12_fit: Directly available: your 5-fold CV already produces 5 checkpoint sets
candidates.neurite_support: Per-pixel, so neurite-border disagreement is captured
candidates.code: DIY (~100 lines: load 5 ckpts, mean/std) or torch-uncertainty DeepEnsembleModel
candidates.compute: 5x inference per image (~1-5 s on laptop GPU; precompute and cache per image in the offline app)
candidates.small_data_fit: Best uncertainty option at n~70 images: no extra training data needed
candidates.notes: LEGIATE caveat below: a true deep ensemble (5 seeds, full data) is strictly better for the shipped model; CV-fold ensemble is a valid, strong proxy and is what the literature uses, but label it honestly.

candidates.name: MC-Dropout (Kendall & Gal 2017 / Gal 2015)
candidates.what_it_does: ~10-20 stochastic forward passes with dropout on; mean/variance = uncertainty; no extra models needed
candidates.pc12_fit: Zero retraining if the U-Net was trained with dropout (verify rate ~0.1-0.5)
candidates.compute: 10-20x inference; slower than ensemble-of-5 and noisier
candidates.notes: Fallback ONLY if the shipped model must be a single checkpoint (e.g., ONNX size cap). Ensemble is preferred: better calibrated, no stochastic-forward quirks in ONNX export (dropout-in-ONNX works but is fiddly).

candidates.name: TTA disagreement (flip/90deg-rotation)
candidates.what_it_does: Run model on 4 TTA variants, average maps; disagreement = free epistemic signal, works with a single model
candidates.pc12_fit: PC12 neurite direction output is rotation-sensitive, so TTA also acts as a self-consistency check on the angle feature
candidates.notes: Cheap bonus signal to blend into the uncertainty map when only one model is deployed; not a substitute for an ensemble.

candidates.name: Evidential deep learning (Sensoy 2018) / Bayesian U-Net (Kendall 2017)
candidates.what_it_does: Single-pass per-pixel Dirichlet/evidence outputs, or full Bayesian weights
candidates.pc12_fit: Requires RE-TRAINING with new heads/losses — conflicts with 'no training at runtime' + 15-week timeline + ONNX simplicity
candidates.compute: Single pass (evidential) — appealing; Bayesian U-Net needs MCMC/VI sampling = slow
candidates.small_data_fit: Fine, but you pay in engineering, not data
candidates.notes: Skip for the product. Mention in the paper as 'considered and rejected' with the retraining cost + weak segmentation evidence (Tan et al. 2024, TAAI, found evidential error correlations are task-dependent) as justification.

candidates.name: Cellpose prob_map + GUI (product precedent)
candidates.what_it_does: Cellpose outputs a per-pixel cellprob map (0-255) alongside masks; GUI overlays it, human-in-the-loop training workflow lets users fix mistakes and retrain
candidates.pc12_fit: This is the pattern to copy: probability channel as first-class output + overlay + review loop; our neurite prob channel maps 1:1
candidates.neurite_support: Cellbody-centric, but the UI pattern transfers to neurite prob maps
candidates.license: BSD-3-Clause (model weights CC-BY-NC — do NOT bundle Cellpose weights in your app)
candidates.notes: Recommend = adopt the UX pattern. StarDist is the other precedent (per-pixel object probability channel + NMS, https://github.com/stardist/stardist, BSD-3, TensorFlow-based so heavier for a desktop app).

candidates.name: torch-uncertainty
candidates.what_it_does: PyTorch UQ framework: DeepEnsemble/MC-dropout/packed-ensembles wrappers, segmentation tutorials, ECE/reliability-diagram metrics, temperature scaling, selective-classification (failure-detection) metrics — exactly the validation battery we need
candidates.pc12_fit: Covers both the uncertainty stack and the calibration/failure-detection metrics in one package (NeurIPS D&B 2025 paper)
candidates.notes: NOTE: 'pytorch-uncertainty' (the name in the brief) is DEAD — 404 everywhere I tried (jbshr/pytorch-uncertainty, jacobgil/pytorch-uncertainty both 404). torch-uncertainty is the maintained successor. Lightning-based; if that's friction, the 5-model ensemble + ECE are trivial DIY.

candidates.name: NeuroQuantify
candidates.what_it_does: DL cells+neurites from phase contrast + neurite length/orientation quantification (arXiv 2310.10978) — your closest prior work
candidates.pc12_fit: Direct domain precedent; its output set (cells, neurite count/length/orientation) matches the project spec
candidates.neurite_support: Yes — neurite segmentation + skeletonization is its core
candidates.license: Not verified in this session (listed in the brief as known prior work)
candidates.notes: No XAI/uncertainty layer in the paper — that gap is exactly our XAI contribution.

techniques.name: Deletion/insertion curves (saliency validation)
techniques.how_it_helps: The minimum credible saliency check: sort pixels by IG importance, hide (occlude) top-k and re-run model, plot DSC/loss vs k% pixels hidden; compare top-k curve vs random-k; our curve must drop significantly faster
techniques.effort: Low — ~1 day on holdout set (14 images); offline, not app runtime
techniques.notes: Also run a model-swap sanity check per Adebayo et al. 2018: explanations should change with the model. Skip insertion curves (deletion is cheaper and the standard for segmentation).

techniques.name: Per-pixel temperature scaling + ECE/reliability diagram
techniques.how_it_helps: Single scalar per class fit on val logits (torch-uncertainty TemperatureScaler); gives the uncertainty heatmap an honest scale and one figure for the thesis (reliability diagram before/after)
techniques.notes: Full per-pixel calibration (Guo 2017 is classification-only) is NOT worth it: the app consumes RELATIVE uncertainty (which pixels to flag), not calibrated probabilities. One global T per class is the sweet spot; report ECE on labeled pixels as the metric.

techniques.name: Uncertainty-gated review queue
techniques.how_it_helps: Per-cell 'review confidence' = min cellprob + ensemble std inside the mask; sort cells by risk; UI auto-flags low-confidence cells for human check (Cellpose/QuPath-style HITL pattern, without any retraining)
techniques.effort: Medium — it's mostly UI wiring over the two maps we already have
techniques.notes: This is where uncertainty becomes a product feature: the professor sees an actionable workflow, not just a heatmap.

techniques.name: Select/failure-detection metric (AUROC of 'flag' vs error)
techniques.how_it_helps: Prove the uncertainty map actually ranks mistakes: AUROC/precision-recall of flagging pixels (or cells) with top uncertainty vs pixels whose DSC is worst; torch-uncertainty has these metrics built in
techniques.notes: This is the number that answers 'does your uncertainty mean anything?' — pair it with the deletion curves for the XAI chapter.

bold_ideas.idea: Active-labeling loop: run the ensemble on the lab's UNLABELED image archive, rank images by max uncertainty / expected-information-gain, and ask the PI to label only the top ~20 hardest images when batch 2 arrives
bold_ideas.why_now: Unlabeled lab images exist (count unknown) and the ensemble ships anyway; batch-2 ETA ~2 weeks means this fits in the timeline as a 3-day script
bold_ideas.feasibility: High — it's inference + ranking + an export for the labeling tool
bold_ideas.risk: PI may not label the suggested images; fall back to 'uncertainty report' deliverable
bold_ideas.differentiator: Almost no student project closes the uncertainty->data->retraining loop; turns UQ from a figure into a measurable DSC gain (report DSC with and without the 20 extra images)

bold_ideas.idea: Saliency-guided morphometrics QA: flag a cell's neurite-length/angle feature as 'unreliable' when the ensemble disagrees on any pixel along that neurite's skeleton; report per-feature reliability alongside MAE
bold_ideas.why_now: Combines the two pipeline halves (segmentation + morphometrics) that most projects keep separate; directly answers 'how do I trust a single measured neurite angle'
bold_ideas.feasibility: Medium — needs the skeleton from the morphometrics stage (R3 scope), then just sample uncertainty along it
bold_ideas.risk: Skeletized uncertain borders can overstate uncertainty; threshold tuning
bold_ideas.differentiator: Per-FEATURE (not per-image) uncertainty is novel for a thesis-scale app and maps onto their required per-feature error metrics

bold_ideas.idea: ONNX-identical XAI: run Grad-CAM/IG inside the exported ONNX graph (or on the ONNX session) so the desktop app explains the EXACT shipped artifact, not a PyTorch twin
bold_ideas.why_now: ONNX Runtime supports gradients; the team already plans ONNX export — proving XAI-on-ONNX kills the 'but your app runs a different model' objection
bold_ideas.feasibility: Medium — ONNXRuntime gradient API is workable for a U-Net; ViT trickier
bold_ideas.effort: ~3 days spike, drop if stuck (PyTorch twin is the fallback and still defensible)
bold_ideas.risk: Gradient support gaps in specific ops
bold_ideas.differentiator: Very few student projects run attribution on the deployed artifact itself

bold_ideas.idea: TTA self-consistency as a neurite-angle sanity channel: average the 4 rotated-prediction angle estimates; large spread -> angle marked low-confidence (rotation-equivariance check for free)
bold_ideas.why_now: Neurite direction is the feature least protected by everything else in the stack
bold_ideas.risk: Model may not actually be rotation-equivariant; then the spread just measures model inconsistency, still useful
bold_ideas.differentiator: Cheap, defensible, specific to their angle output

bottom_line: Minimum-credible XAI+uncertainty stack (<=3 methods, all offline, all <~2 s/image on a laptop GPU): (1) **Integrated Gradients** (captum, ~20 steps, per-pixel target = pixel logit) as the saliency layer, shown as a red-yellow overlay answering 'why is this pixel neurite'; (2) **5-member ensemble** (the 5 CV folds as members) for per-pixel epistemic uncertainty, shown as a blue heat overlay + per-cell review-confidence bar that gates a human review queue; (3) **one global temperature per class** (torch-uncertainty) so the uncertainty has an honest scale, reported with a single ECE + reliability diagram. CV-folds-as-ensemble: LEGITIMATE but with an asterisk — Kirscher et al. (MICCAI 2026, arXiv 2605.18329) show CV-fold ensembles are valid uncertainty proxies (they even track inter-rater ambiguity) but are worse at calibration and failure detection than a true deep ensemble (5 seeds, same data); since compute is free, ship a true 5-seed ensemble on the full 70-image set as the deployed model and keep the CV-fold ensemble as the validation-benchmark — never average a fold's predictions on its own validation fold (that IS leakage). Saliency validation to demo: deletion curves (occlude top-k IG pixels vs random-k, plot DSC drop) on the holdout fold + one Adebayo-style model-swap sanity check. Skip: Seg-Grad-CAM (Keras, dead), evidential/Bayesian U-Nets (retraining cost, weak segmentation evidence), SHAP (too slow per-pixel). Note: 'pytorch-uncertainty' is a dead package — use torch-uncertainty.
